chose: While home's deploy record (state.json) can't be read, the run totals (home_deploy_runs{outcome}, home_deploy_pulls, home_deploy_pulled_bytes) are held as last read, in the gauge sweep's memory. DeployFailed keeps main's increase() rule, so it sees the reset when the deploy that heals the record rolls back, however long the gap. After a restart nothing was read, so the totals are absent until a tick reads them. The last run's time and exit code, the newest epoch and the marker's age, which state a current value, are NaN. Unreadable is still told: home-deploy/read_state is held open (invariant 9), and HomeFailuresOpen fires after about two hours. The bound: if file_host restarts while the record is unreadable and the healing deploy rolls back more than an hour after that restart, DeployFailed doesn't see it (HomeFailuresOpen has fired for the record by then). The coordinator chose this on CONS-NEXT's raise, after three review rounds on server#1208's branch kept finding faults in NaN on the totals.
options: NaN on the totals, and DeployFailed bridges the gap with increase(last_over_time((x == x)[7d:5m])[1h:1m]): a gap on the graph, a nested subquery each evaluation, and a record unreadable more than 7 days before the healing deploy still hides its rollback

gray: The owner chose on server#1207 that a failed reading empties a gauge rather than freezing it at its last value, and on #1208 that an unreadable record is 'left absent rather than 0'. This reads the #1207 rule as covering gauges that state a current level (renders, drive, last pass), not running totals, where the last value read stays true as a lower bound; the owner may read it otherwise.
undo: Put NaN back on the totals (record_state sets f64::NAN when the record is an error, and Last.totals goes) and use the first option's rule for DeployFailed, with a promtool case on a gap of two hours or more.
